deities: Hanuman (Chamatkarik Hanumanji - rare reclining/sleeping posture, ~8-10 ft idol; also called Ichhapurti Hanuman, the wish-fulfilling Hanuman)

history.dynasty: Unknown (folk/pilgrimage shrine; revenue records mention a Mahavir Hanuman shrine under a peepal tree about 100 years ago - verify)
history.period: Local tradition says centuries old; the documented shrine is about a century old (verify); one low-reliability source claims 1000 years (verify)
history.summary: Jam Sawali is a popular Hanuman pilgrimage shrine in Sausar tehsil, Chhindwara district, Madhya Pradesh (the CSV 'state' column holds the town name 'Chhindwara' - the real state is Madhya Pradesh). Its main claim is a rare reclining (sleeping) Hanuman idol under a peepal tree, said to be the only such sleeping-posture Hanuman in India. Legend: the idol stood upright facing east; treasure-seekers tried to uproot it (20 oxen could not move it) and the idol 'lay down' on its own. Another legend ties the site to the Ramayana - Hanuman resting under a peepal tree while carrying the Sanjivani herb (legend only, not history). A stream of water is said to flow continuously from the idol's navel and is distributed as prasad. Devotees come for relief from evil influences/black magic and for wish fulfilment; special pujas are held on purnimas, Ramnavami and Hanuman Jayanti. Men may approach the idol closely while women take darshan from a distance, per temple committee norms. Sources disagree on exact antiquity - flag as unverified.

name: Jam Sawali Hanuman Temple
town: Jam Sawali (Sausar tehsil; CSV town 'Chhindwara' is the district HQ, ~60-65 km away)
town_description: Jam Sawali (also spelled Jam Savli/Jamsavli) is a village in Sausar tehsil of Chhindwara district, Madhya Pradesh, on the Nagpur-Chhindwara corridor about 60 km from both Chhindwara and Nagpur. The temple, managed by a devasthan committee, has lodging, parking, shops and eateries nearby; devotees usually stay in Chhindwara or Nagpur. Rush days are Tuesday and Saturday.

travel.airport: Nearest major airport is Nagpur (~70-90 km - verify); Jabalpur is a farther alternative.
travel.railway: Nearest railheads are Pandhurna / Sausar Road locally (verify); Nagpur Junction is the major railhead.
travel.road: On the Nagpur-Chhindwara highway, ~60-65 km from Chhindwara and ~60 km from Nagpur; buses and taxis run from both (per visitor reviews).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March (pleasant weather); Tuesdays and Saturdays see heavy crowds.
visitor_information.opening_hours: One low-reliability source lists 4:00 AM - 9:00 PM daily (verify); timings not officially published - confirm with temple trust before visiting.
